name: End-to-End Sequential Consistency
description: An approach to providing end-to-end sequential consistency for a language, enforced jointly by an SC-preserving variant of the LLVM compiler and modified x86 hardware. To curb the overhead it enforces SC only for accesses to shared mutable variables, classifying memory regions as thread-local, shared-immutable, or shared-mutable via a combination of static compiler analysis and hardware-assisted dynamic analysis. Reported overhead is 6.2% on average (17% maximum) versus stock LLVM and x86. Like the other SC-preserving designs it admits exactly the SC behaviours.

irm.note: SC-for-DRF compiler/runtime; inverse roach motel sound for SC-for-DRF per Poetzl & Kroening §4.

catSupport.note: The programmer-visible model is SC, which sc.cat states exactly; the content of the proposal is the compiler and hardware enforcement, which cat does not describe.
